consumer.status: schema is a proposal (types.cairo header: ranges finalized in consumer issues #1-#3)

settings.type: u8 percent of full scale 0..=100, suggested 40

settings.engine: setTimbre(m, n, p) after quality is applied (setQuality resets all programs/drums)
setTimbre n; program[n] or drummap[n-35] (47 entries); out-of-range n is silently ignored
setTimbre p (array of operator objects); no engine limit; built-ins use at most 4

operator.type: u8: 0 out, 1..=10 FM of op route, 11..=18 AM of op route-10
operator.engineSemantics: 0: to channel volume; 1..10: FM into o[g-1].frequency (or playbackRate/440 for an n* target); >10: AM into gain of op g-11; target must already exist (earlier op) or note-on throws

operator.conversion: Sine 'sine', Square 'square', Sawtooth 'sawtooth', Triangle 'triangle', WhiteNoise 'n0', MetallicNoise 'n1', Harmonics -> registered 'w...' name (#26, proposed), Samples -> registered 'n...' name (#26, proposed)

operator.engineSemantics: output op: v * velocity^2/16384 * 2^((note-60)/12*k); FM: depth Hz = v * target op freq (* key scaling); AM: depth = v (no velocity scaling)
output op freq = noteFreq*t + f; FM/AM modulator freq = targetOpFreq*t + f
linear ramp 0 -> level over a; a=0 sets level at note-on
setTargetAtTime(s*level, t+a+h, d); d=0 jumps; drums stop at t + 3.5*d of operator 0
per-op setTargetAtTime(0, off, r); voice end = off + 3.5*r of operator 0 for all ops; ignored on rhythm channels
if p != 1: frequency (or playbackRate) setTargetAtTime(start*p, note-on, q)

waveform.engine: proposed setHarmonicWave(name, real, imag) (#26); precedent _createWave: real all 0, imag[0]=0 (DC), imag[i]=harmonic i; w9999 -> real [0,0,0,0,0], imag [0,9,9,9,9]
waveform.conversion: imag = [0, h[0], ..., h[n-1]] (length n+1 <= 65), real = zeros(n+1)

waveform.engine: proposed setSampleWave(name, samples) (#26), buffer looped at playbackRate = freq/440

filter.consumer: Filter.cutoff u32 fixed: Hz 20..=20000 or multiple 0.25..=16

filter.engine: fq (#27) -> BiquadFilterNode.Q (dB for lowpass/highpass, linear for bandpass)

questions.Q1: Harmonics: element 0 is harmonic 1 while Web Audio index 0 is DC; confirm imag (sine) vs real placement, whether u16 is a raw relative amplitude or /10000 fixed-point, that unsigned values cannot express sign/phase (e.g. alternating-sign triangle series), and that the engine limit counts 65 coefficients for 64 harmonics.
questions.Q2: Samples: the i8 -> float map is ambiguous (x/128 gives -1..0.9922; x/127 gives -1.0079..1; affine gives -1..1 with 0 -> 0.0039). The consumer promises exact sample-and-hold chip waves; #26's contract only promises preserved character within measured tolerances (buffer playback interpolates).
questions.Q3: Filter Q: consumer q is a unitless 0.1..30; Web Audio lowpass/highpass Q is in dB, bandpass Q is linear. Pick linear Q with a documented LP/HP conversion, or per-type native values.
questions.Q4: Filter key tracking: basis (note frequency with tuning, or operator frequency note*t+f; bend and pitch envelope excluded for a fixed filter). 16x key-tracked cutoffs exceed 22,050 Hz for notes >= 89 at 44.1 kHz, and a fixed 20 kHz cutoff exceeds Nyquist below 40 kHz; a clamp policy is needed.
questions.Q5: Reverb: percent -> reverbLev = reverb/100 is implied by the 30 <-> 0.3 defaults, but setReverbLev multiplies by 8 (default wet gain 2.4; 100% -> 8.0). '0 turns reverb off' could mean setReverbLev(0) (convolver stays in the graph) or useReverb:0 (constructor-only, no convolver).
questions.Q6: Master volume: percent of full scale -> masterVol = master_vol/100 (out gain) is implied; full scale 1.0 is twice the engine default 0.5. Confirm the mapping and whether >0.5 is intended to be reachable.
questions.Q7: Modulator frequency: the Cairo doc says note_frequency*ratio+offset_hz for every operator; the engine uses the target operator's frequency for FM/AM operators (measured 2645 Hz vs 1325 Hz by the doc formula).
questions.Q8: Voice lifetime uses operator 0 only: melodic voices end at note-off + 3.5*r[0]; drum voices stop at note-on + 3.5*d[0] and ignore note-off, release and sustain; a drum with d[0]=0 is silent. The Cairo doc describes release per operator.
questions.Q9: Drum slots 35..81 match the engine's 47-entry drummap; GM2 notes outside it are unreachable, and drum timbres sound only on rhythm channels (channel 10 unless GS SysEx changes it). Confirm 35..81 stays the contract.
questions.Q10: Voices: the engine prunes released notes before the oldest held ones, drums are not stored as voices, and each drum hit prunes melodic voices to voices-1. The consumer doc says the oldest note is cut.
questions.Q11: Range coverage: consumer d/r max 10.0 excludes built-in values 11 and 12 (39 operator fields in 32 built-in timbres across program0/program1/drummap1); every other built-in value fits and is exact at 1e-4. Decide whether built-ins must be re-expressible.
questions.Q12: Route 9-10 cannot target anything with at most 8 operators; targets must be earlier operators or note-on throws.
questions.Q13: Determinism: the consumer's consistency claim fails at b70ba90 for every sound when reverb > 0, not only noise waveforms, because the reverb impulse is also Math.random (#7 default-seed policy).
questions.Q14: Quality must be passed as a Number: setQuality('0') installs the quality-1 tables because a non-empty string is truthy.
questions.Q15: setTimbre keeps and mutates the caller's arrays (fills defaults in place); the consumer page should pass fresh objects.
questions.Q16: Lifecycle: the constructor always creates an AudioContext (internalcontext has no option) and plays a velocity-1 warm-up note; the consumer's tap-to-start page has to construct inside the gesture or rely on resume() in send() (#12).
